title: The Boeing Company FY2022 Form 10-K — Item 1. Business: four reportable segments and segment definitions
key_points: Boeing states it is organized based on the products and services it offers and operates in four reportable segments: Commercial Airplanes (BCA), Defense, Space & Security (BDS), Global Services (BGS), and Boeing Capital (BCC).

BCA 'develops, produces and markets commercial jet aircraft principally to the commercial airline industry worldwide'; the in-production family includes the 737 narrow-body model and the 767, 777 and 787 wide-body models; production of the 747 wide-body ended in 2022; development continues on the 777X program and the 737-7 and 737-10 derivatives.

BDS engages in 'the research, development, production and modification of manned and unmanned military aircraft and weapons systems for strike, surveillance and mobility', including fighter and trainer aircraft, vertical lift (rotorcraft and tilt-rotor), commercial derivative aircraft (anti-submarine and tanker), strategic missile and defense systems, C4ISR, cyber and information solutions, and satellite systems including government and commercial satellites and space exploration.

BGS 'provides services to our commercial and defense customers worldwide' and sustains aerospace platforms and systems with supply chain and logistics management, engineering, maintenance and modifications, upgrades and conversions, spare parts, pilot and maintenance training systems and services, technical and maintenance documents, and data analytics and digital services.

BCC seeks to ensure Boeing customers have the financing needed to buy and take delivery of Boeing product while managing overall financing exposure; its portfolio consists of equipment under operating leases, sales-type/finance leases, notes and other receivables, assets held for sale or re-lease and investments.
raw_excerpt: We are organized based on the products and services we offer. We operate in four reportable segments: • Commercial Airplanes (BCA); • Defense, Space & Security (BDS); • Global Services (BGS); • Boeing Capital (BCC). ... This segment develops, produces and markets commercial jet aircraft principally to the commercial airline industry worldwide. ... This segment provides services to our commercial and defense customers worldwide. BGS sustains aerospace platforms and systems with a full spectrum of products and services, including supply chain and logistics management, engineering, maintenance and modifications, upgrades and conversions, spare parts, pilot and maintenance training systems and services, technical and maintenance documents, and data analytics and digital services.

title: Boeing 2022 10-K — Commercial aircraft program inventory and 787/777X program status
key_points: Boeing paused 777X-9 production during 2022 and 2023 and expensed $325 million of abnormal production costs in 2022; the 777X program had near break-even margins at December 31, 2022.
A $3,460 million reach-forward loss on the 787 program was recorded in Q4 2021 as a reduction to deferred production costs.

At December 31, 2022 the 787 program carried $12,689 million of deferred production costs, $1,831 million of supplier advances, and $1,722 million of unamortized tooling and other non-recurring costs.
These program-level dollar amounts are inventory/cost balances, not program revenues.
raw_excerpt: In April 2022, we decided to pause production of the 777X-9 during 2022 and 2023. ... We expensed abnormal production costs of $325 during the year ended December 31, 2022. The 777X program has near break-even margins at December 31, 2022. ... The resulting reach-forward loss of $3,460 was recorded as a reduction to deferred production costs.

Arithmetic (not a source claim): United States = 39,218/66,608 ≈ 58.9% of total revenues, i.e. a single category above 20% under the geographic taxonomy.

Revenues from the U.S. government (including foreign military sales through the U.S. government), primarily recorded at BDS and BGS, represented 40% of consolidated revenues in 2022 (49% in 2021, 51% in 2020).
Arithmetic (not a source claim): the U.S. government customer category at 40% is a single category above 20% under a customer-type taxonomy.
The 10-K states these disaggregated tables are presented because they 'best depict how the nature, amount, timing and uncertainty of our revenues and cash flows are affected by economic factors.'
raw_excerpt: Revenues, including foreign military sales, are reported by customer location and consisted of the following: … Asia $8,393 $5,845 $5,931 … Total non-U.S. revenues 27,374 23,196 21,677 / United States 39,218 39,076 36,979 … Total revenues $66,608 $62,286 $58,158 … Revenues from the U.S. government (including foreign military sales through the U.S. government), primarily recorded at BDS and BGS, represented 40%, 49% and 51% of consolidated revenues for 2022, 2021 and 2020, respectively.

title: The Boeing Company FY2022 Form 10-K — BCA and BDS revenues by customer location (p.111)
url: kb_demo/financebench/pdfs/BOEING_2022_10K.pdf · p115（BCA revenues by customer location; BDS revenues by customer location）
key_points: BCA FY2022 revenue from contracts with customers by customer location: Asia $4,484M; Europe $4,038M; Middle East $2,003M; Other non-U.S. $3,042M; Total non-U.S. $13,567M; United States $12,167M; total $25,750M; total segment revenues $25,867M.
BDS FY2022 revenue from contracts with customers by customer location: U.S. customers $17,144M; Non-U.S. customers $6,018M; total $23,162M.
BDS revenue from the U.S. government was 89% of segment revenue in 2022 (89% in 2021 and 2020); BDS revenue recognized over time was 99% and on fixed-price contracts 60%.
BCA revenue was 100% recognized at a point in time and 100% on fixed-price contracts in 2022.
Arithmetic (not a source claim): BCA's United States category = 12,167/66,608 ≈ 18.3% of total company revenues (below 20%); BDS's U.S. customers = 17,144/66,608 ≈ 25.7% (above 20%).

title: The Boeing Company FY2022 Form 10-K — BGS revenues: commercial vs government split (p.112)
url: kb_demo/financebench/pdfs/BOEING_2022_10K.pdf · p116（BGS revenues consisted of the following）
key_points: BGS FY2022 revenue from contracts with customers: Commercial $9,560M; Government $7,681M; total $17,241M; intersegment revenues eliminated on consolidation $370M; total segment revenues $17,611M.
BGS revenue was 50% recognized at a point in time, 88% on fixed-price contracts, and 33% from the U.S. government in 2022.

Arithmetic (not a source claim): BGS Commercial = 9,560/66,608 ≈ 14.4% and BGS Government = 7,681/66,608 ≈ 11.5% of total company revenues — under this finer commercial/government split no single category exceeds 20%.
BGS backlog at December 31, 2022 was $19,338M; total company backlog was $404,381M.

title: The Boeing Company FY2022 Form 10-K — BGS Results of Operations: segment share of total company revenues (p.38)
key_points: BGS revenues were $17,611M in 2022, $16,328M in 2021 and $15,543M in 2020.
The 10-K itself states BGS revenues were 26% of total company revenues in 2022 (26% in 2021, 27% in 2020).
BGS earnings from operations were $2,727M with operating margins of 15.5% in 2022.
